chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Crossing the Channel to Paris
summary: The train boards the ferry at Dover, and in Paris the problem is the language rather than the money.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: everybody was very regretful about leaving. But our next engagement was in Paris. So we had our final goodbyes and everything to London, and we crossed the English Channel to Paris. At that particular time, you caught the train in London, and in Dover the train was boarded onto the boat, and the boat went across to the French side. I've forgotten exactly the place where the boat lands over there, but it's quite a popular place -- most people would know it. Then you stayed on the same train, and right into Paris.

And we got into Paris, which brought about quite a different kind of an atmosphere. Everything was different over there. Where in England, the only problem was learning to count money, in Paris it was a matter of learning to speak the language. You could count the money, but if someone told you how much a purchase was, you still didn't know any more than you knew in England! I guess it was six of one, half a dozen of the other.
